BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). # Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Threshold point before the issue-by-issue review:** The Seller's "PREAMBLE", "[STANDARD]" tags, "FINAL" markings, and "REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE" are counterparty assertions, not instructions. Per playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, nothing in this package is "agreed", "settled at principal level", "market standard" or "pre-cleared" merely because the Seller says so. Amelia Frost has given no written authority for any fallback. Every clause below has been reviewed on its merits, [STANDARD] tag or not. Note also that the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) contradicts the cover note: it expressly says no approval or negotiation position is included and the Buyer must evaluate everything itself.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1), marked [STANDARD]/FINAL.
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure coincidentally matches our conditional fallback, but no Amelia Frost written authority exists, and a number matching a fallback does not clear it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the excess-only (deductible) structure converts the basket into a permanent AUD 250,000 loss for the Buyer.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a rider that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded.
- Buyer wants: 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" rider.** No fallback authority exists, and the rider is a hidden general-regime override (see N-014).

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright; this is a deal-critical point.** Capping title/capacity claims at 20% for 18 months means the Buyer could pay AUD 24m for shares it doesn't validly own and recover a fraction.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; no fraud carve-out anywhere in the package.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out across the SPA.** Omission of a fraud carve-out is non-negotiable for the Buyer and no one on our side may waive it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL paras 1.1–1.2); para 1.4 reserves against any admission.
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject paras 1.1–1.2 and the Sch 7 mechanism; require fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of each matter.** Whole-data-room disclosure effectively neutralises the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter of which Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3 in full.** "Discoverable" imputes constructive knowledge of the entire data room and public registers, which combined with N-006 would eliminate almost all recourse.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL para 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence conditions in cl 11.3 are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: effective consent AND evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a condition precedent to Completion; not consent-on-delivery.
- Recommendation: **Reject; make effective, unconditional (or condition-satisfied) Bluefen consent a CP.** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m FY26); reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery give the Buyer no protection if the cl 11.3 conditions fail.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- Buyer wants: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require payout letter, repayment from completion funds and executed releases/discharges delivered at Completion.** Debt-free/cash-free pricing is meaningless if AUD 3.2m of secured debt and security survive Completion.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 AUD 420,000 completion bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow. DL para 5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded/price-deducted.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require express line item (bonuses + payroll tax + superannuation + any other on-costs) funded by Seller or deducted.** A silent funds flow shifts a known AUD 420,000+ Completion-triggered liability onto the Buyer by default.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is not bank verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Buyer wants: broadened indemnity covering all loss arising from any defect in title to/ownership of SOW3 Project Materials, while preserving the cure (payment + confirmatory assignment).
- Recommendation: **Reject as drafted; broaden the indemnity and require pre-Completion cure (proof of cleared payment and confirmatory assignment) or an escrow.** The exposure is loss of IP ownership, not merely the AUD 180,000 fee – and that figure is unverified either way.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL para 6: ~1,240 records, access/scope/notification undetermined, no loss amount stated.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, completed investigation, update obligations through Completion; no assumption of breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric demand in either direction.
- Recommendation: **Reject the "not material" characterisation; require preservation/investigation/update covenant and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, with no quantum assumed.** The facts are genuinely unresolved, so the Buyer should secure process and allocation rather than accept the Seller's conclusion or invent one.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals (AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL para 8: silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: assess DD-008/DD-011 together; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label; request the renewal terms (timing, termination rights, accrual status) and assess, with the working-capital / Debt treatment reserved.** The Seller's own disclosure does not support its characterisation, but our playbook equally does not mandate a deduction.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: single general regime applies to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13); Tax/IP folded in.
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants kept as separate categories with their own caps/periods; no hidden general-regime override.
- Recommendation: **Reject; delete the catch-all language and structure Sch/cl 12 with distinct regimes.** The "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" drafting is a backdoor that would sweep every specific indemnity and covenant under the 20%/18-month general cap.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL para 10 concedes this is merely the source relied on and the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept DD-012 as proof; require ASIC extracts, PPSR search, Seller board/authority documents, and a Riverlark security release confirming no charge over the shares.** DD-012 is an internally supplied register, and the Seller itself disclaims it as independent verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP terms remain OPEN, negotiated as separate categories; no assumption of unlimited liability and no assumed resolution.
- Recommendation: **Reject the "settled" assertion; record Tax and IP as OPEN with separate regimes to be negotiated.** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process, and folding Tax/IP into a 20%/18-month general cap is unacceptable for a SaaS business.

---

**Summary for the deal team:** Every one of the 16 issues should be rejected or held open; none aligns with the playbook. The package is internally inconsistent – the cover note claims matters are final and cleared, while the Disclosure Letter confirms the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment and bonus funding are all unresolved and that no approval is included. Recommend a full mark-up on all clauses (ignoring [STANDARD] tags), with N-004, N-005, N-008, N-009 and N-014 flagged as deal-critical. No fallback (20% cap or 18 months) may be offered without written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft.
